title: [BUG] Documentation not up-to-date
body:
## Environment
- Platform (select one):
  - [x] Anthropic API
  - [ ] AWS Bedrock
  - [ ] Google Vertex AI
  - [ ] Other: <!-- specify -->
- Claude CLI version: 0.2.67 (Claude Code)
- Operating System: ubuntu-24
- Terminal:  Terminal App 

## Bug Description
using 'claude -p' and Claude runs into permissions issues:

content": [
    {
      "type": "tool_result",
      "content": "Claude requested permissions to use Replace, but you haven't granted it yet.",
      "is_error": true,
      "tool_use_id": "toolu_014sFdBK2QB3jBFJj5yu1Nmv"
    }
  ]

There is not Replace listed in the documentation...

## Steps to Reproduce
Do something that requires Claude to use the Replace tool... 

## Expected Behavior
The tool is documented so I can properly grant permission. 
If the permission is not granted Claude should fail gracefully with an appropriate and understandable message to the user - instead Claude keeps going and just writes what would have been replaced into the conversation. This is another example of Anthropic just ringing the cash register with Claude chewing up tokens doing actions that do not satisfy the prompt ot the user expectation - which, obviously, needed to replace something. As a user how am I supposed to know any such permission is needed if it is not documented.

## Actual Behavior
Claude tries to perform the action but fails and just keeps going..

## Additional Context
Claude admitted that the Replace command was know to it from the system message. 

you gave me this message - Claude requested permissions to use Replace, but you haven't granted it yet.  What tool exactly is this?

● Read(CLAUDE.md)…
  ⎿  Read 98 lines (ctrl+r to expand)

● The Replace tool is used to completely overwrite the contents of a file. It takes two parameters:
  - file_path: The absolute path to the file you want to write
  - content: The new content to write to the file

  This is different from the Edit tool, which makes specific changes within a file. Replace is useful when you need to create a new file or completely rewrite an existing one.

> how do I grant permission?

● When you see the permission request in Claude Code, you need to respond with a command that grants the permission:

  For example, use:
  <command-name>grant-tool-permission</command-name><command-message>grant-tool-permission Replace</command-message>

  This grants permission for Claude to use the Replace tool. You can similarly grant permissions for other tools when requested.

> no, I mean what is it called? It isn't documented. I know about FileReadTool and FileWriteTool for example, but is it just ReplaceTool?

● I see the confusion. The tool is simply called "Replace", not "ReplaceTool".

  In Claude Code, the official tool names are:
  - View (for reading files)
  - Edit (for making specific changes to files)
  - Replace (for completely overwriting files)
  - Bash (for running shell commands)
  - GlobTool (for finding files by pattern)
  - GrepTool (for searching file contents)
  - LS (for listing directory contents)

  When you need to grant permission, you would use:
  <command-name>grant-tool-permission</command-name><command-message>grant-tool-permission Replace</command-message>

> /allowed-tools 

> where did you find that help? it is not on the official docs page at https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/claude-code/overview

● Fetch(https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/claude-code/overview)…
  ⎿  Request failed with status code 403

● You're right - I apologize for the confusion. The tool information I provided comes from my understanding of the available tools in this conversation, not from the official documentation. I was looking at the functions available to me in this
  environment as shown in my system instructions, not from the public documentation.

  The tool names I listed are the ones I can actually invoke in this session (View, Edit, Replace, Bash, GlobTool, GrepTool, LS, etc.). These may differ from what's documented in the official Claude Code documentation.

> well, since al
